summary: Run a server-side FileMaker script with a JSON parameter.
purpose: Use this when you want a reviewed server-side script example and need the generated parameter format spelled out clearly.
learningGoals: Understand that FileMaker scripts are server-side operations with side effects outside simple CRUD.
See the existing Data API script helper output preserved exactly.
Make transport limitations explicit instead of implying OData parity.
explanation: Scripts can do far more than read or write one field, so this module stays code-only. It teaches the safe parameter shape while making clear that script execution belongs in reviewed server-side flows.
commonMistakes: Assuming a script is harmless because the request payload looks small.
Expecting an OData transport to provide the same script path as the Data API helper.
Passing real customer data into learning examples.
expectedResult: You get a reviewed script starter snippet, but the playground will not run it live.

safety.confirmationText: Scripts may have broad side effects. Review the script name, parameter, and environment before running this code.

prerequisites: Know exactly what the target FileMaker script does in the current environment.
Use scrubbed demo parameters instead of real customer data.

inputs.label: Script name
inputs.help: Use the exact FileMaker script name you want to run.

inputs.label: Script value
inputs.help: This becomes the value inside the starter JSON parameter object.

php:odata.reason: This version preserves the original Playground guidance and does not claim an OData script block.
php:odata.example:
// FileMaker scripts use the Data API route.
// Switch to Data API to generate an executable script example.

javascript:data-api.reason: Browser playground testing is intentionally read-only. FileMaker scripts must stay in reviewed server-side code.

javascript:odata.reason: FileMaker scripts are not offered as a browser OData playground action. Switch to the PHP Data API variant for a reviewed server-side example.

beginner: Scripts can do many things at once, so this module generates code only.
Use a scrubbed demo parameter while learning.
If you need a runnable example, switch to the PHP Data API variant and review it on the server.
advanced: The OData PHP branch intentionally stays comment-only to preserve the old generator behavior and avoid false parity.
Restricted safety is appropriate because scripts may create, edit, delete, or trigger secondary workflows.
No browser variant is supported because the learning surface stays read-only by design.
